agents.name: JD Edwards Adaptive Fulfillment Advisor
agents.description: Read-only JDE fulfillment advisor that learns connection details and operational corrections through ordinary work conversations.
agents.connection_context: Environment, role, and device headers come from the current conversation or relevant prior context. Basic Auth remains environment-local.
agents.memory_description: The user works normally and corrects the agent one rule at a time; relevant corrections are applied silently in a fresh chat.
capabilities: Learns required connection context when it is first needed.
Adapts to incremental corrections about priority, inactive status, donor reserve, and approvals.
Uses relevant prior feedback naturally without asking users to manage memories.
prerequisites: Private Agent Factory 26.7-compatible environment with Agent Memory and cross-thread sharing enabled.
Network access to JDE AIS plus an available LLM connection.
JDE Basic Auth user with read access to F4211, F4201, F41021, F4311, F4101, and F0101.

demo_sessions.title: Session 1 — work normally and correct incrementally

steps.speaker: User
steps.text: Can you check our backorders and tell me what we should tackle first?

steps.speaker: Expected agent
steps.text: Ask only for the missing JDE environment, role, and device identifier.

steps.speaker: User
steps.text: Use JPS920 with the *ALL role and ops-fulfillment-demo as the device ID. Those are our normal connection settings for JDE orders, backorders, fulfillment, and inventory.

steps.speaker: User
steps.text: That is not how our team triages this. Start with the earliest requested line that is still active, not the largest-value order, and treat status 900 lines as inactive.

steps.speaker: User
steps.text: Also, never recommend cross-branch stock if the donor would fall below 1,000 units after the move. Show the arithmetic.

steps.speaker: User
steps.text: Anything that changes JDE needs my approval. Rework the recommendation and keep it read-only.

steps.speaker: User
steps.text: Can you review today's backorders, tell me what we should tackle first, and give me the best cross-branch backup if its local branch cannot cover it? Show me the numbers and keep it aligned with how our team operates.

expected_outcomes: The fresh chat does not ask again for relevant connection values.
Status-900 lines are excluded and the earliest requested active line is prioritized.
Donor-floor arithmetic is explicit and approval remains mandatory.
The response ends with: JDE changes made: none (read-only analysis).
agents.validation_environment: JPS920 sample data, clean memory then two chats
validation_notes: Learned records are deliberately excluded from the workflow and release archive.

steps.speaker: User
steps.text: Find up to five sales order lines with backordered quantity and explain which one is the best recovery candidate.

agents.name: JD Edwards Fulfillment Memory Agent
agents.description: Read-only JDE fulfillment analysis with an explicitly named connection and recovery profile recalled across chat sessions.
agents.connection_context: The end user supplies environment, role, and device values; the agent recalls them from a named operating profile. Basic Auth remains environment-local.
agents.memory_description: The user deliberately establishes a named profile, then the agent recalls its connection context and operating policy in a fresh chat.
capabilities: Recalls a user-specific JDE execution context across sessions.
Recalls and enforces an explicitly named recovery policy.
Shows post-transfer donor-cushion arithmetic before recommending cross-branch stock.
Keeps every JDE-changing action behind explicit human approval.

steps.speaker: User
steps.text: Hi, I'm taking over the North America fulfillment review. Let's call this the North America Fulfillment Standard. For this JDE connection, use environment JPS920, role *ALL, and device ops-fulfillment-demo. Please remember that for future chats. I'm only setting up today, so don't query JDE yet.

steps.speaker: User
steps.text: One more rule for that standard: a cross-branch candidate is eligible only when it addresses the earliest requested active line and leaves at least 1,000 units of indicative available balance in the donor branch after the proposed allocation. Anything that could change JDE needs explicit human approval. Please remember that too.

steps.speaker: User
steps.text: Morning. Which JDE environment is saved in my North America Fulfillment Standard? Answer from memory only; do not query JDE.

steps.speaker: User
steps.text: What role and device identifier are saved for that same standard? Answer from memory only; do not query JDE.

steps.speaker: User
steps.text: Before we look at today's orders, remind me of the saved cross-branch eligibility rule and the approval control for that standard. Please do not query JDE yet.

steps.speaker: User
steps.text: Great—use that remembered standard to run today's fulfillment exception review. Find up to five backordered sales-order lines, determine which order deserves investigation first, and recommend the single best eligible cross-branch recovery action. Show the post-allocation cushion arithmetic and do not change JDE.

expected_outcomes: The fresh chat recalls all connection values and policy constraints.
Donors below the remembered 1,000-unit floor are rejected with arithmetic.
The analysis makes no JDE changes.
agents.validation_environment: JPS920 sample data, same user across two chats
validation_notes: Agent Memory retrieval is user-specific and relevance-based.

The earliest requested active line wins; status-900 lines stay out.
Ineligible donors are labeled with explicit post-transfer arithmetic.
Applied from your prior feedback lists relevant business rules without exposing memory internals.
The follow-up preserves the approval and authorized-execution boundary.
